title: `Texture2D.draw_rect` rendering at low resolution and with dark outline on HiDPI displays
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in v4.7.dev [2af785641ae249573f45eb61852d22e0b1a8a03c] - Reproducible in v4.6.1.stable.official [14d19694e] ### System information Godot v4.7.dev (a761ad537) - macOS Tahoe (26.3.1) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - Apple M4 Pro - Apple M4 Pro (14 threads) - 24.00 GiB memory ### Issue description Attempting to draw an SVG texture on a HiDPI display using the `Texture2D.draw_rect()` method gives a blurry result. Here is an example from my [code actions PR](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/114168): In addition, when the editor is in light mode, there is some strange gray outline around the icon (perhaps due to some antialiasing technique?): Both of these are the result of the following C++ code: ```cpp theme_cache.code_action_icon->draw_rect(p_canvas_item, p_icon_rect, false, use_color); ``` with `p_canvas_item` being the output of `TextEdit.get_text_canvas_item()` and `use_color` being the yellow color of the icon. ### Steps to reproduce Attempt to call the `Texture2D.draw_rect()` method with a small SVG icon on a HiDPI screen. The icon will appear blurry/pixellated. If drawn on a light background, dark artifacts will be visible around the icon. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) The call to `draw_rect()` in my code actions PR is here: https://github.com/Meorge/godot/blob/a761ad5374bc4cf0559039b417be3f25669bfbcb/scene/gui/code_edit.cpp#L490 I've also attempted to create an MRP using pure GDScript. It renders the same lightbulb icon using several different methods. In the `draw_rect()` method (and related methods), the same resolution and artifact issues can be seen: [mrp-draw-texture_2026-03-29_21-02-45.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26338651/mrp-draw-texture_2026-03-29_21-02-45.zip)
